title: Annual ALOHA trap means exclude the nutrient increment, but deployment mixtures fit with a 14.17-fold weight cap under uniform release
abstract: We test whether sinking-particle composition can match the 1988-1996 to 2009-2024 ALOHA oxygen, nitrate and phosphate increment on density 26.4-26.6. The nitrogen to phosphorus increment ratio is 12.337. No mixture of 36 annual trap mean compositions fits. Mixtures of 305 measured 150 m deployments do fit when the common oxygen to carbon factor is free from 1.0 to 1.6. A linear program proves that the smallest maximum ratio of fitted to reference phosphorus weight is 14.173. An independent sorted-allocation proof gives the same bound. The reference gives each sampled year equal weight before its phosphorus flux is used. A conditional year-block resample gives a 95 percent bound range of 7.14-28.26, with the particle library fixed. Removing any one of four very low nitrogen to phosphorus deployments retains a fit; removing all four excludes it. This is a finite-library composition test under uniform element release and fixed preformed composition. It has no flux, depth, chronology or transport constraint and does not identify a cause. Annual averaging can remove feasible compositions and give too strong an exclusion. Code, aggregate results, input hashes and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Deployment composition counts, the annual mean nitrogen to phosphorus range, and the interior increment. The sharp weight cap uses the joint oxygen, nitrogen and phosphorus constraints.
